previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with redness, swelling, and pain in his right second toe, which had been chronically discolored and previously lost its nail. He was at high risk for infection due to recent autologous stem cell transplant. Initial treatment included IV vancomycin for suspected MRSA. Imaging revealed bony destruction concerning for osteomyelitis. After lack of improvement, podiatry performed an incision and drainage, followed by a more extensive debridement. Foot culture grew coagulase-negative staphylococcus, sensitive to vancomycin. Vascular studies showed adequate perfusion despite moderate peripheral vascular disease. Anticoagulation was transitioned from heparin back to warfarin. The patient improved clinically, was transitioned to oral minocycline, and discharged home with crutches, non-weight-bearing on the right foot, and instructions to continue outpatient medications including aspirin for secondary prevention.

Brief Hospital Course:
A/P:  ___ man with multiple myeloma, COPD, CAD, s/p autologous 
stem cell transplant ___, admitted with fever, cough, and 
myalgias.  
.
#  Fever/Cough: The patient's original presentation was 
concerning for PNA, RSV, or flu.  Nasal washings were done for 
influenza, RSV, and parainfluenza.  He was empirically treated 
with Tamiflu and Rimantidine.  His CXR could not rule out a RML 
PNA so he was started on ceftriaxone and azithromycin.  On 
hospital day 1 his washing came back RSV + and tamiflu and 
rimantidine were discontinued.  A non contrast CT was done which 
found bronchiolitis likely secondary to his RSV and no focal 
consolidation.  His ceftriaxone was discontinued and he was 
discharged on azitrhomycin with the plan to finish a total of a 
seven day course.  He was also discharged on his normal 
inhailers and albuterol given that he had some wheezes on exam.  
His lung exam was also positive for crackles at the bases.  He 
had a normal oxygen saturation at rest and with ambulation prior 
to discharge and he stated that he felt back to his baseline 
level of health.  At the time of discharge his blood cx and his 
urinary probe for GC and chlamydia were both still pending.
.
#Drop in cell lines: He has a drop in all his cell lines during 
his hospitalization which could be due to his RSV or due to his 
antibiotics.  His bactrim was also held for one day so that he 
would have adequate folic acid to make cells.  His bactrim was 
restarted at discharge.  His cell lines were increasing on the 
day of discharge.  He will come to the ___ clinic to get 
his blood drawn on ___ prior to seeing his PCP.  Then he 
will follow up with ___ on the afternoon of ___.
.
#  CAD/PVD:  He was continued on aspirin and Toprol XL as per 
his out-patient regimen.
.
#  Afib:  He was continued on his Toprol and warfarin per his 
out-patient regimen.  His INR was therapeutic during his 
hospitalization.  He should have close follow-up on his INR as 
an outpatient given that he is being discharged on azithromycin.
.
#  Pain:  He was continued on his out-patient oxycodone pain 
regimen.
.
#  FEN: He was on a cardiac diet and his lytes were repleted as 
needed.
.
#  PPx:  Bactrim, Acyclovir, ambulation, therapeutic INR, and 
insentive spirometry.
